answer_1.quote: We develop a novel reference‑free framework to explore bias in open‑ended generation tasks... We generate questions, answers and perturbations to evaluate NLG outputs.
answer_1.outputs: pairwise preference scores and Attack Successful Rate (ASR) values

answer_2.quote: We quantify biases by ASR, which is the percentage of samples with preference shifted towards the perturbed answer... we do not employ traditional automatic metrics such as BLEU or ROUGE.

answer_3.quote: Our experiment also involves the evaluation of some representative models, including GPT‑4o, Claude‑2, Claude‑3, Gemini‑Pro, GPT‑4‑Turbo, GPT‑3.5‑Turbo, LLaMA2‑70B‑Chat, Mixtral‑7Bx8‑Instruct, Spark and Qwen. ... We form two groups ... control group ... experimental group ... and ask the LLMs to vote which answer is better.

answer_4.quote: We employ 60 college students as our human judges... Each judge is instructed to determine whether "Answer 1" is better, "Answer 2" is better, or a "Tie", based solely on the semantic quality of the answers.
answer_4.guideline: Judges focus exclusively on the semantic quality of the answers, ignoring tone, format, or answer order; they may select "not familiar" or "Tie" when appropriate.
